title: Stream checkpoint tokens and explicit retry signals for client SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Customers frequently build low-latency streaming features (chat, audio->text, live summarization) that need robust client-side recovery semantics. Current SDKs surface generic transient vs terminal errors but lack a standardized way to attach stream-specific resume checkpoints and retry signals. This leaves application teams to implement ad-hoc resume logic, increasing latency, cost, and engineering support burden.

Goal: Define and implement a cross-language SDK contract for: 1) attaching opaque stream checkpoint tokens to streaming responses; 2) surfacing explicit retry signals and backoff hints on exceptions and stream completions; 3) ergonomic client APIs for resuming a stream from a checkpoint in Python, TypeScript, and Go. The contract must be compatible with existing server-side resume endpoints and secure by default.

Proposed contract (high-level):
- StreamCheckpoint: a short opaque token emitted periodically in the stream envelope (field name: "stream_checkpoint"), and also returned in terminal responses. Tokens are to be treated as opaque by clients; servers guarantee they represent a consistent internal KV-cache state.
- Resume API: streaming clients may call the same generation endpoint with parameter "resume_from_token": "<token>", and server will fast-forward internal KV cache where possible to continue generation.
- RetrySignal metadata on exceptions (SDK-level exception metadata): {"code": "E_STREAM_TRANSIENT|E_STREAM_TERMINAL|E_RATE_LIMIT", "retryable": "true|false", "backoff_hint_ms": "integer (ms)", "resume_token": "optional token"}.
- Exception types: introduce StreamResumeSuggestedError (includes resume_token), StreamFatalError, and StreamBackoffError (contains backoff_hint_ms). Language SDKs map these to idiomatic exceptions/errors while preserving the metadata accessible as properties.
- Idempotency and security: resume_token must be revocable and short-lived (TTL <= 5 minutes) when tied to user-sensitive context. All resume operations must require the same API key/credentials that opened the original stream.

Compatibility and ergonomics:
- Python: generator-based streaming helpers yield (chunk, checkpoint) tuples and raise StreamResumeSuggestedError with .resume_token metadata. Provide helper method stream.resume(resume_token, **kwargs).
- TypeScript: AsyncIterable<{chunk: string, checkpoint?: string}>; thrown errors include .metadata property. Provide sdk.stream.resume(resumeToken, opts).
- Go: stream channel of structs {Data string; Checkpoint string}; errors implement interface ResumeToken() string and BackoffHint() time.Duration.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (Python, TS, Go) implement the contract and expose resume helpers and typed errors.
- E2E integration test: simulate mid-stream transient interruption; client successfully resumes and completes with <= 2x steady-state token cost.
- Docs: Confluence design doc and code examples published; Console telemetry emits checkpoint metrics for at least 90% of resumed streams.

Trade-offs considered:
- Keeping tokens opaque avoids coupling server implementation but reduces debuggability; mitigation: provide an optional debug endpoint that expands tokens for internal troubleshooting behind RBAC.
- Short TTL reduces risk but increases chance of stale tokens; mitigation: allow explicit server-provided lease-renewal in long-lived sessions.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Design and API spec (this ticket) + security review (1 week).
2) Add checkpoint envelope and retry metadata to runtime (runtime PR).
3) SDK surface & language mappings + small examples (2 sprints).
4) E2E tests & canary rollout (1 sprint).

Related artifacts and links: see links field for docs, example snippets, and experimental PRs.
